did_you_know.text: Did you know? Ezekiel describes a holy tract of land 25,000 long and 10,000 wide, dedicated to the LORD throughout its entire area.
Did you know? Within the consecrated area, a 500-by-500 square is set apart for the temple, with an open space 50 cubits wide surrounding it.
Did you know? From the sacred measure, an additional area 25,000 long and 10,000 wide is measured, and within it stands the temple, described as the Most Holy Place.
Did you know? The holy area is intended for the priests who serve in the temple, providing them with a place to live and a consecrated place for their service.
Did you know? The Levites receive an allotment 25,000 long and 10,000 wide, containing twenty chambers for their service.
Did you know? The prince is allotted land to the west and east of the sacred offering and the city's property, so that he may have an inheritance in the land.
Did you know? The chapter sets a clear moral boundary for the princes: they must no longer oppress the people, but must leave the land to the tribes of Israel.
Did you know? Ezekiel commands the princes to remove violence and robbery and to practice justice and righteousness.
Did you know? The chapter defines the maneh using three weights: 20 shekels, 25 shekels, and 15 shekels—a total of 60 shekels.
Did you know? The offerings are set at precise rates: one-sixth of an ephah from a homer of wheat and barley, and one-tenth of a bath from a kor of oil.
